{"decision": "APPLY", "workflow_yaml": "name: CI            # shows as “CI” in the Actions tab

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:      # runs on every PR

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # The unit suite takes ~4 min; fail fast instead of stalling until the
    # runner is lost (seen once on 3.12, run 42357449207).
    timeout-minutes: 20

    strategy:
      matrix:
        python-version: ["3.10", "3.11", "3.12", "3.13"]

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}

      - name: Cache pip dependencies
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/pip
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-pip-${{ matrix.python-version }}-${{ hashFiles('pyproject.toml') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-pip-${{ matrix.python-version }}-

      - run: python -m pip install --upgrade pip
      - run: pip install -e .[dev]            # adjust extras as needed
      - run: pytest tests/unit -q             # unit tests only; integration tests need a frida-server

  # Cross-file version-guard. Prevents the silent frida-major bump bug
  # described in issue #63: any PR that bumps the frida major in
  # requirements.txt without bumping the friTap major in friTap/about.py
  # fails this job. See RELEASING.md and dev/check_compat.py.
  version-guard:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 2          # need HEAD~1 for the drift diff

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"

      - run: pip install pyyaml
      - run: python dev/check_compat.py

  # Legacy-install resolution check. Verifies each constraints/<era>.txt
  # file resolves cleanly against its top-of-era PyPI release without
  # backtracking. Uses --dry-run so no actual install happens; this is
  # pure resolver work and runs in well under a minute per cell. Catches:
  # a constraints file being deleted, a top-of-era PyPI version being
  # yanked, or a new frida release breaking the era's lower bound.
  legacy-constraints-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # python-version × era cross product; `include` only maps each era
        # to its top-of-era PyPI version (matched by `era` key, expansion only).
        python-version: ["3.11", "3.13"]
        era: ["frida15", "frida16", "frida17-legacy"]
        include:
          - era: frida15
            version: "1.3.3.3"
          - era: frida16
            version: "1.4.3.0"
          - era: frida17-legacy
            version: "1.6.3.1"
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
      - run: python -m pip install --upgrade pip
      - run: |
          pip install --dry-run \
            "fritap==${{ matrix.version }}" \
            -c "constraints/${{ matrix.era }}.txt"

  # Reproducible agent rebuild. Asserts that running ./dev/compile_agent.sh
  # against the pinned toolchain (npm ci honors package-lock.json,
  # frida-compile/typescript/@types/frida-gum exact-pinned in package.json)
  # produces a byte-identical friTap/fritap_agent.js. If it diverges, either
  # the committed agent is stale (run dev/compile_agent.sh and commit the
  # result) or the toolchain pin needs tightening.
  agent-build-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "22"

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"

      - name: Install pinned toolchain (lockfile-enforced)
        # --ignore-scripts skips package.json::prepare (which re-runs
        # frida-compile). The explicit `./dev/compile_agent.sh` step below
        # is the one we diff against, so building twice is pure waste.
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts
      - name: Fetch frida native binding
        # --ignore-scripts also skips frida's own install script, which
        # downloads build/frida_binding.node that frida-compile imports.
        run: npm rebuild frida

      - name: Install frida-tools (provides frida-pm)
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install "frida-tools>=14.0.0,<15.0.0"

      - name: Rebuild agent
        run: ./dev/compile_agent.sh

      - name: Verify committed agents match rebuild
        # ./dev/compile_agent.sh (bare) rebuilds BOTH the intercept and the
        # memscan bundle; both are tracked, so both must be byte-identical to a
        # fresh rebuild from agent/.
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- friTap/fritap_agent.js friTap/fritap_memscan.js; then
            echo "::error ::A committed agent bundle does not match a fresh rebuild from agent/. Run ./dev/compile_agent.sh locally and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Run agent unit tests (main + memscan)
        # The .mjs harness self-compiles an -B iife bundle via
        # node_modules/.bin/frida-compile (present after `npm ci`); test:agent
        # runs the Node test runner over the TS unit tests via tsx.
        run: |
          npm run test:agent
          npm run test:memscan-agent

      - name: Build manifest
        run: |
          {
            echo "## Agent build manifest"
            echo "frida-compile: $(node -p "require('frida-compile/package.json').version")"
            echo "node: $(node --version)"
            echo "agent SHA-256: $(sha256sum friTap/fritap_agent.js | awk '{print $1}')"
            echo "agent size: $(wc -c < friTap/fritap_agent.js) bytes"
          } | tee BUILD_MANIFEST.txt

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: agent-build-manifest
          path: BUILD_MANIFEST.txt

  # Public-tree leak guard (tiering §F, L1). Reproduces the §E publish strip
  # (private.txt) and asserts the result carries nothing private: no agent/signal,
  # no private protocol selectable via --protocol, no public module importing a
  # stripped path, and a NAME-FREE SHA-256 denylist scan (scripts/denylist.hashes;
  # the cleartext terms never ship). HARD failures fail the build immediately;
  # the accepted bare-'signal' reveal-token residuals (api.py/TUI functional
  # coupling + the shared SIGNALKEYLOG format string) keep the scan at exit 2.
  # DECISION (§F-strict, 2026-06): exit 2 is the intended steady state, NOT a
  # TODO — the HARD structural/dist rules are the contract; the token scan is a
  # guide (operational-privacy stance). rc==2 passes the job by design.
  leak-guard:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"

      - run: python -m pip install --upgrade pip
      - run: pip install -e .[dev]

      - name: Public-tree leak guard
        run: |
          set +e
          bash scripts/check_public_denylist.sh
          rc=$?
          set -e
          if [ "$rc" -eq 1 ]; then
            echo "::error ::Leak guard HARD violation: private code/protocol present in the public tree."
            exit 1
          elif [ "$rc" -eq 2 ]; then
            echo "::notice ::Leak guard PASS-structural: accepted bare-'signal' reveal-token residuals remain (operational-privacy stance; the HARD structural/dist rules are the contract). Exit 2 is the intended steady state."
            exit 0
          elif [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then
            echo "::error ::Leak guard errored (rc=$rc)."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "Leak guard clean."

  # friTap-import smoke test against the supported frida version(s).
  # Today the matrix is length-1 (frida 17.x is the only supported major
  # per compat.yml). When the next frida MAJOR ships AND friTap bumps to
  # match (RELEASING.md / version-guard enforce the pairing), add a row
  # here. Keep the OLD frida version in the matrix for one minor cycle as
  # a deprecation window.
  smoke-import:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        frida-version: ["17.9.6"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"

      - run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install -e .
          pip install "frida==${{ matrix.frida-version }}"

      - name: Import smoke test
        run: |
          python -c "import friTap; print('friTap', friTap.__version__)"
          python -c "from friTap.backends.frida_backend import FridaBackend; FridaBackend()"", "rationale": "The workflow repeatedly installs Python dependencies (pip install -e .[dev], pip install pyyaml, pip install frida-tools, pip install -e .) across several jobs, including a 4-cell Python matrix in the test job, with no dependency cache. P-LIT-GHA-CACHE reports a modest VM-time reduction from caching dependency downloads and its preconditions are met: repeated dependency fetching is measurable and pyproject.toml is available as a cache input. The measured experiment example adds actions/cache@v4 for ~/.cache/pip keyed on pyproject.toml before dependency installation. Applying the same mechanism to the test job preserves every build/test step and required check (caching only avoids re-downloads), weakens no permissions, and adds no secrets, publishing, deployment, or new network access.", "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE", "experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-ae496965ffa682a2-r2"]}

name: CI            # shows as “CI” in the Actions tab

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:      # runs on every PR

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # The unit suite takes ~4 min; fail fast instead of stalling until the
    # runner is lost (seen once on 3.12, run 42357449207).
    timeout-minutes: 20

    strategy:
      matrix:
        python-version: ["3.10", "3.11", "3.12", "3.13"]

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}

      - name: Cache pip dependencies
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/pip
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-pip-${{ matrix.python-version }}-${{ hashFiles('pyproject.toml') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-pip-${{ matrix.python-version }}-

      - run: python -m pip install --upgrade pip
      - run: pip install -e .[dev]            # adjust extras as needed
      - run: pytest tests/unit -q             # unit tests only; integration tests need a frida-server

  version-guard:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 2          # need HEAD~1 for the drift diff

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"

      - run: pip install pyyaml
      - run: python dev/check_compat.py

  legacy-constraints-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # python-version × era cross product; `include` only maps each era
        # to its top-of-era PyPI version (matched by `era` key, expansion only).
        python-version: ["3.11", "3.13"]
        era: ["frida15", "frida16", "frida17-legacy"]
        include:
          - era: frida15
            version: "1.3.3.3"
          - era: frida16
            version: "1.4.3.0"
          - era: frida17-legacy
            version: "1.6.3.1"
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
      - run: python -m pip install --upgrade pip
      - run: |
          pip install --dry-run \
            "fritap==${{ matrix.version }}" \
            -c "constraints/${{ matrix.era }}.txt"

  agent-build-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "22"

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"

      - name: Install pinned toolchain (lockfile-enforced)
        # --ignore-scripts skips package.json::prepare (which re-runs
        # frida-compile). The explicit `./dev/compile_agent.sh` step below
        # is the one we diff against, so building twice is pure waste.
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts
      - name: Fetch frida native binding
        # --ignore-scripts also skips frida's own install script, which
        # downloads build/frida_binding.node that frida-compile imports.
        run: npm rebuild frida

      - name: Install frida-tools (provides frida-pm)
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install "frida-tools>=14.0.0,<15.0.0"

      - name: Rebuild agent
        run: ./dev/compile_agent.sh

      - name: Verify committed agents match rebuild
        # ./dev/compile_agent.sh (bare) rebuilds BOTH the intercept and the
        # memscan bundle; both are tracked, so both must be byte-identical to a
        # fresh rebuild from agent/.
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- friTap/fritap_agent.js friTap/fritap_memscan.js; then
            echo "::error ::A committed agent bundle does not match a fresh rebuild from agent/. Run ./dev/compile_agent.sh locally and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Run agent unit tests (main + memscan)
        # The .mjs harness self-compiles an -B iife bundle via
        # node_modules/.bin/frida-compile (present after `npm ci`); test:agent
        # runs the Node test runner over the TS unit tests via tsx.
        run: |
          npm run test:agent
          npm run test:memscan-agent

      - name: Build manifest
